description: Health of Trickster's application load balancers: pool failover and floor state, member load and ejections, fanout failures, sticky sessions and autodiscovery. Row 1 answers whether any ALB is degraded now.

panels.title: ALB 5xx share
panels.description: Share of client requests to the selected ALBs answered with a 5xx status, over the last rate interval. It includes the 502 an ALB returns when its pool has no eligible member and the 5xx answers its members pass through. Only requests addressed to an ALB backend are counted, not the sub-requests it sends to members (unless a member is itself an ALB). Idle ALBs read 0; "no traffic" means no selected ALB has served a request since Trickster started.

targets.expr: ((sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", provider="alb", backend_name=~"$alb", http_status="5xx"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / (sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", provider="alb", backend_name=~"$alb"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)) or (0 * sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", provider="alb", backend_name=~"$alb"}[$__rate_interval]))) or vector(-1)

panels.title: ALBs on backup
panels.description: ALBs whose pool is sending traffic to its backup: true members right now because no primary member is eligible. 0 is healthy. Only ALBs with backup members report this, and an ALB counts when any selected instance has failed over (each instance decides from its own health view). A reload that removes every backup member of an ALB that was on backup leaves it counted until Trickster restarts.

targets.expr: sum(max by (backend_name) (trickster_alb_pool_on_backup{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$alb"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Floor overrides
panels.description: ALBs whose healthy_floor is not applied as written: lowered to 0 because healthy_floor is 1 and some members have no health check, or set below 0 so members confirmed Failing stay in the pool. Both are configuration warnings rather than outages; the Pool flags table names the ALB and flag.

targets.expr: count(max by (backend_name) (trickster_alb_pool_floor_reset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$alb"}) == 1 or max by (backend_name) (trickster_alb_pool_admits_failing{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$alb"}) == 1) or vector(0)

panels.title: Draining members
panels.description: Pool members draining right now: marked drain: true, or discovered members their provider reports as terminating. A draining member takes no new work and keeps only its sticky sessions. Expected during rollouts; a member that stays draining is usually leftover configuration.

targets.expr: count(max by (alb_name, member) (trickster_alb_member_draining{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Member ejections
panels.description: Passive-health ejections over the time range. alb.stream.passive_health ejects a member for its eject period (30 s by default) after consecutive connect failures (3 by default) on a stream listener; HTTP traffic never ejects. 0 when passive health is not configured.

panels.title: Fanout failures
panels.description: Member responses that failed inside fr, fgr, nlm and tsm fanouts over the time range, all ALBs combined (the metric has no ALB label): panics, truncated or short bodies, clone failures, capture-budget fail-fasts and TSM merge failures. TSM's no_contribution reason is left out because it re-counts these and also counts non-2xx member answers.

panels.title: Sticky refused
panels.description: Requests, connections or native sessions refused over the time range because their pinned member was unavailable and the ALB sets sticky.on_unavailable: reject. With the default (repick) this stays 0 and moved sessions show as repick in the Sticky sessions row.

panels.title: Discovery errors
panels.description: Autodiscovery problems in the last 15 minutes: provider refresh, poll or watch errors (recovered refresh panics included), plus snapshots rejected by min_members or applied only in part because some members failed to build. The ALB keeps its last-good membership meanwhile. 0 when autodiscovery is not configured.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(trickster_discovery_refresh_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", discoverer=~"$discoverer"}[15m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(trickster_alb_discovery_snapshots_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", discoverer=~"$discoverer", result=~"rejected|partial"}[15m])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Requests/s by ALB
panels.description: Client requests per second addressed to each ALB backend. The requests the ALB sends on to its members are counted again under the members' own backend names and are not included here, except where a member is itself an ALB. user_router ALBs have no pool gauges, so they appear only while the ALB variable is All.

panels.title: 5xx share by ALB
panels.description: Share of each ALB's client requests answered 5xx: the ALB's own 502 when no pool member is eligible plus member 5xx answers passed through. Gaps mean the ALB had no requests in the interval. Dashed lines mark 1% and 5%.

targets.expr: (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", provider="alb", backend_name=~"$alb", http_status="5xx"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", provider="alb", backend_name=~"$alb"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", provider="alb", backend_name=~"$alb"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Backup failover
panels.description: Whether each ALB's pool dispatches to its primary members or to its backup: true members, which take traffic only while no primary member is eligible. Only ALBs with backup members appear. Shows the worst state across the selected instances. A reload that removes every backup member leaves the old series at its last value until restart.

panels.title: Draining members
panels.description: When each pool member was draining (drain: true, or terminating per its discovery provider). Blank means not draining, and members that never drained are not listed. A discovered member that drains for less than a scrape interval during a rollout may not show; Member churn in the Autodiscovery row records its removal.

panels.title: Pool flags by ALB
panels.description: One row per ALB with a member pool (every mechanism except user_router), worst value across instances; ALBs removed by a reload linger until restart. On backup is blank for ALBs without backup members. healthy_floor reset: the floor is 1 but some members have no health check, so 0 applies, re-checked whenever discovery changes the pool. Admits Failing members: healthy_floor is below 0.

panels.title: Pool ALBs
panels.description: Number of selected ALBs that have a member pool (every mechanism except user_router). Use it to confirm the expected ALBs are loaded; an ALB removed by a config reload is still counted until the process restarts.

targets.expr: count(max by (backend_name) (trickster_alb_pool_floor_reset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$alb"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Pool refresh panics
panels.description: Panics recovered while an ALB pool rebuilt its list of eligible members, over the time range, all ALBs combined (no ALB label). The pool keeps serving its previous list, so health changes stop affecting routing until a rebuild succeeds. Any non-zero value is a bug worth reporting with logs.

panels.title: In-flight work by member
panels.description: Requests, stream connections and native sessions in flight to each pool member, summed across instances, for the 20 busiest members. Only p2c, lc and lt ALBs track in-flight work, so other mechanisms have no series. Sampled at scrape time, so bursts between scrapes are not visible.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (alb_name, member) (trickster_alb_member_inflight{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb"}))

panels.title: In-flight imbalance by ALB
panels.description: Busiest member's in-flight count minus the idlest member's, per p2c, lc or lt ALB, summed across instances. Near 0 means work is spread evenly; a lasting gap means a member is slow or favoured (lt prefers fast members by design). Backup and draining members take no new work and pull the minimum toward 0.

targets.expr: max by (alb_name) (sum by (alb_name, member) (trickster_alb_member_inflight{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb"})) - min by (alb_name) (sum by (alb_name, member) (trickster_alb_member_inflight{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb"}))

panels.title: Passive-health ejections
panels.description: Ejections per member per interval. alb.stream.passive_health (on rr, p2c, hrw, lt or lc) ejects a member after consecutive connect failures on a stream listener, for its eject period. Ejections refused by max_ejected_percent are not counted, the last live member is never ejected, and readmission is not recorded.

panels.title: Member status
panels.description: Per member: work in flight now (p2c, lc and lt ALBs only), passive-health ejections over the time range, and whether it is draining. A member appears only if at least one of these applies to it, so members of rr or hrw ALBs that were never ejected or drained are not listed.

panels.title: Fanouts/s by mechanism
panels.description: Scatter calls per second by mechanism, all ALBs of a mechanism combined (there is no ALB label); fgr ALBs are counted under fr. A call happens only when two or more members are live, since one member is proxied directly, so this is below the ALB request rate. A TSM query that needs several partial aggregates (avg, stddev, ...) counts once per variant.

panels.title: Shard failures/s by reason
panels.description: Failed member responses per second inside fanouts. truncated: body over max_capture_bytes; short_read: body ended before its Content-Length; routing_flap: either of those after the member fell below Passing; aggregate_cap: fail-fasted by max_fanout_capture_bytes; clone: request copy failed; panic: member handler panicked; merge: a TSM variant failed to merge (the request gets a 502); no_contribution: a TSM member or replica group gave nothing usable, re-counting the others and including non-2xx answers.

panels.title: Failing shards per fanout
panels.description: Average number of failed member responses per scatter call (panic, aggregate_cap, clone, short_read and truncated failures divided by fanouts). It is not a percentage and can exceed 1, since one call to N members can lose several. routing_flap, merge and no_contribution are left out to drop health-flap noise and double counting.

targets.expr: (sum by (mechanism) (rate(trickster_alb_fanout_failures_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", mechanism=~"$mechanism", reason=~"panic|aggregate_cap|clone|short_read|truncated"}[$__rate_interval])) or (sum by (mechanism) (rate(trickster_alb_fanout_attempts_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", mechanism=~"$mechanism"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0)) / (sum by (mechanism) (rate(trickster_alb_fanout_attempts_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", mechanism=~"$mechanism"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Loser drain time
panels.description: How long the losing members of an fr or fgr fanout kept running after the winner was chosen: the time it takes cancellation to reach a slow upstream. This is background work, not client latency. Persistently high values mean upstreams ignore cancellation, which piles up goroutines and connections. Buckets run from 1 ms to 30 s; losers that finished before the winner are not timed.

panels.title: Loser drain distribution
panels.description: Number of losing fr or fgr fanout members by how long they kept running after the winner was chosen, per interval. Expect roughly one observation per extra live member per winning fanout. Mass above 1 s means cancellation is not reaching upstreams promptly.

panels.title: Losers still running after 1 s
panels.description: Share of losing fr or fgr fanout members whose request was still running 1 s after the winner was chosen. Should stay near 0: the HTTP transport cancels losers as soon as a winner is claimed. Dashed lines mark 5% and 20%.

targets.expr: 1 - (sum by (mechanism) (rate(trickster_alb_fanout_loser_drain_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", mechanism=~"$mechanism", le=~"1|1.0"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (mechanism) (rate(trickster_alb_fanout_loser_drain_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", mechanism=~"$mechanism"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Session outcomes/s
panels.description: Requests, stream connections and native sessions through ALBs with alb.sticky (rr, p2c, lc, lt or hrw), by how their session fared. hit: sent to its pinned member; miss: no token or table entry, so every new client is a miss; repick: pinned member unavailable, moved; rejected: refused by on_unavailable: reject. Traffic that reaches no member is not counted.

panels.title: Pinned sessions honored
panels.description: Of the sessions that arrived already pinned and valid, the share sent to their pinned member (hit / (hit + repick + rejected)), per ALB. Below 100% means pinned members were unavailable, so sessions moved or were refused. New clients (miss) and bad tokens are not part of this ratio.

targets.expr: sum by (alb_name) (rate(trickster_alb_sticky_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", result="hit"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (alb_name) (rate(trickster_alb_sticky_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", result=~"hit|repick|rejected"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Moved, refused and bad-token sessions/s
panels.description: The troublesome session outcomes per ALB. expired and invalid occur only in cookie or header mode (table mode reports an expired entry as miss); invalid means a malformed or foreign token. Without a shared sticky.secret, each process signs with its own key, so invalid spikes after every restart and persists across replicas behind one address.

panels.title: Sticky table entries (largest instance)
panels.description: Entries in each ALB's sticky table on the instance holding the most, since tables are per process and table.max_entries (100000 by default) applies to each. Present for sticky.mode: table and for sticky ALBs on stream or native listeners. Includes expired entries not yet removed; a reload that changes the table's options starts it empty.

panels.title: Discovered members
panels.description: Members each ALB currently holds from its alb.discovery block, draining members included and static pool entries excluded; highest value across instances. A rejected snapshot (min_members) leaves the last-good count. The series appears after the first applied snapshot and restarts at each reload.

targets.expr: max by (alb_name, discoverer) (trickster_alb_discovery_members{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", discoverer=~"$discoverer"})

panels.title: Member churn
panels.description: Discovered members added and removed per interval. Every instance discovers the same changes itself, so this shows the highest count across instances rather than the sum. A member whose address or replica_group changed is rebuilt and counts as both; members that failed to build are not counted.

panels.title: Snapshots by result
panels.description: Membership snapshots processed per interval, highest count across instances. applied: membership updated; partial: applied, but some members failed to build; rejected: below min_members, so the last-good pool is kept. Providers drop unchanged snapshots before they get here, so this moves only when membership changes or on reload.

panels.title: Refresh errors/s by discoverer
panels.description: Failed provider refreshes, polls or watch events per second, by discoverer and provider: transport and status errors, bad documents, DNS failures, Kubernetes list or watch failures, and recovered panics. The last-good membership is kept. This, not the time since the last snapshot, is the reliable discovery health signal.

panels.title: Discovery status by ALB
panels.description: Per discovery-backed ALB: members now (highest across instances), how many members the instances disagree by, time since the last applied or partial snapshot, and snapshots rejected or applied in part over the time range. The time since the last snapshot grows while membership is stable, so it is not a staleness signal; use refresh errors for that.

targets.expr: max by (alb_name, discoverer) (trickster_alb_discovery_members{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", discoverer=~"$discoverer"})

max by (alb_name, discoverer) (trickster_alb_discovery_members{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", discoverer=~"$discoverer"}) - min by (alb_name, discoverer) (trickster_alb_discovery_members{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", discoverer=~"$discoverer"})
time() - max by (alb_name, discoverer) (trickster_alb_discovery_last_refresh_success_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", discoverer=~"$discoverer"} > 0)

sum by (alb_name, discoverer) (increase(trickster_alb_discovery_snapshots_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", alb_name=~"$alb", discoverer=~"$discoverer", result=~"rejected|partial"}[$__range]))

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: The Prometheus-compatible data source that scrapes Trickster's /metrics endpoint.

list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: Scrape job(s) holding the Trickster targets.

list.name: alb
list.label: ALB
list.description: ALBs to show, from the pool gauges that every ALB except user_router exports. Panels titled (all ALBs) come from metrics without an ALB label and ignore this choice.

list.name: mechanism
list.label: Mechanism
list.description: Fanout mechanism (fr, nlm or tsm; fgr ALBs report as fr). Filters the Fanout row and the fanout tile.

list.name: discoverer
list.label: Discoverer
list.description: Autodiscovery discoverers (entries of the top-level discovery section). Filters the Autodiscovery row.

title: Trickster / Load Balancing
